Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${sin}^{2}$ term: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =\frac{x}{4},$ we have

$$
1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{4}).
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{4})-1+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})-1+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2}){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
